column3: Directly parallels the condemned asking to return so they can perform righteous deeds after recognition.
States that Fire's inhabitants seek to leave but cannot, directly defining the focus's blocked exit.
Places repentance and righteous action within the still-open path back to God, before the focus's request becomes impossible.
Closely repeats the belated wish to be returned and do other than one's former deeds.
The immediately preceding ayah establishes unrelieved punishment in the Fire that the focus's cry inhabits.
A clear messenger has already come, framing why remembrance at the final moment is too late.
Shows wrongdoers facing punishment asking for a short delay to obey the call and follow messengers.
Its rejected pledge to follow a warner sharpens the focus's account of a warner already ignored.
Links tasting punishment with the absence of a helper, though in a distinct hypothetical case.
Joins entrance into the Fire with the wrongdoers' lack of helpers.
Divine knowledge of what is within breasts offers a local basis for the judgment but adds no exit or warning scene.
Defines the revealed book as both warning and reminder, the opportunity referenced in the focus.
Depicts self-wronging people denying their evil actions at death, only to have their deeds fully known.
Directly explains the granted delay as a measured term that ends when its appointed time arrives.
A disregarded prohibition becomes directly tasted consequence, anticipating the focus's final command to taste.
Directly repeats the plea to be taken out, coupled with a promised end to wrongdoing.
The fixed communal term supplies the temporal boundary after which delay cannot be obtained.
Turning people from God's way culminates in tasted evil and great punishment.
Contrasts ineffective worldly status with faith and righteous action as the basis for recompense.
Continued disbelief increases loss before the Lord, extending the local moral-accounting sequence.
The upright Book warns of severe punishment while promising a good reward for righteous deeds.
The oppressed seek an earthly exit and a helper, a limited contrast to the Fire's closed exit and absent aid.
The local mention of angelic messengers provides only a broad setting for the focus's coming warner.
Pairs faith and righteous deeds with an enduring reward, showing the positive alternative to former evil action.
States plainly that wrongdoers have no helper, matching the focus's final denial of aid.
Places the condemned under direct trial in the Fire, supplying the punitive setting.
Its purpose that people remember gives a general counterpart to the focus's missed remembrance.
The direct command to taste and the increase of punishment closely echo the focus's final verdict.
Evil plotting returns upon its authors and prior patterns do not change, reinforcing irreversible consequence.
The messenger's long life among the people supports the focus's claim that sufficient lifetime preceded the warning.
Directly links forgotten encounter, former deeds, and the repeated command to taste enduring punishment.
The secure residents' praise after sorrow has gone does not clarify the condemned cry in the Fire.
God as guide and helper for a messenger is a distant contrast to the wrongdoers' lack of assistance.
Divine knowledge and the absence of helpers for wrongdoers touch accounting only indirectly.
States the final principle that each self is repaid only for what it used to do.
The morning raid has no material connection to warning, judgment, righteous action, or failed exit.
Explicitly identifies the speaker as a clear warner, one of the opportunities named in the focus.
Calls people to inspect the ends of earlier deniers, making historical warning available before judgment.
After the matter is decided, even the source of temptation cannot answer cries for help.
Combines recompense for acquired deeds with the direct command to taste punishment.
The fatigue-free permanent dwelling of the saved is only a remote contrast to the focus's punishment.
Includes both the vain wish for another return and the declaration that Fire's inhabitants cannot leave.
The instruction on acceptable charitable spending does not materially illuminate the focus.
A command is met with refusal and increased aversion, paralleling the rejection of guidance before final consequence.
The lack of a responder to cries and of rescue provides a close image of failed help.
Sets evil deeds' equivalent recompense against the Paradise reward for faithful righteous action.
The comparison of seas and their benefits does not clarify the focus's judgment scene.
Describes turning away from remembrance after it had already arrived, directly matching the missed warning.
On the decisive day, a person remembers what he strove for, making past action unavoidable evidence.
States that every self is repaid for what it earned without injustice on the judgment day.
Repeated failed promises of support clarify the focus's final absence of effective help.
Links shown signs with the capacity to remember through turning back, defining a response still possible before judgment.
The true revealed Book and God's awareness form the local ground for the warning and assessment.
Directly develops the meaning of a granted lifetime by showing its eventual reversal in old age.
Gentle warning is given so that remembrance or fear may arise while response remains possible.
A prayer for truthful entry, exit, and supporting authority is a constructive contrast to the focus's denied exit and help.
A reminder comes through a messenger to warn, invite caution, and open the way to mercy.
The report of one submitting household offers no clear relation to the focus's warning or punishment.
The inherited Book differentiates self-wronging from measured and foremost good action within the local passage.
The distinction between the straight path and failed paths is a broad counterpart to the focus's moral outcome.
The command to taste punishment is explicitly joined to warnings previously given.
The delayed event is held only until a counted term, reinforcing the focus's bounded opportunity.
Satanic deception and altering creation do not add a specific connection to the focus's final plea.
Contrasts knowing revealed truth with blindness and identifies remembrance as the mark of understanding.
The enemy's invitation leads its followers toward companionship in the Blaze, supplying a local causal path.
Empty worship is followed by the command to taste punishment because of disbelief.
After rejecting the warning, the offenders receive the direct command to taste punishment.
Defines the messenger's role as witness, bearer of good news, and warner.
The accusation concerning sexual conduct does not materially illuminate the focus.
Disobedience to divine command and taking an enemy as ally offer only a broad moral parallel.
Evil earnings receive equivalent recompense; no protector remains, and the people of the Fire abide there.
The question exposes the complete collapse of mutual assistance at the point of judgment.
Calls for worship, forgiveness, and repentance while the Lord is near and responsive, the open alternative before finality.
Its contrast between violence and being among reformers only distantly touches doing good instead of prior acts.
Change in a people's condition after inner change is a distant counterpart to the focus's wish to change past conduct.
Faith and righteous deeds receive lasting Garden reward, supplying the positive alternative to condemned former action.
The messenger is a clear warner even though the timing of the event remains with God.
Faith and righteous action receive the fairest recompense and an eased command.
When punishment arrives, the only remaining plea is the admission that they had been wrongdoers.
A coming destructive sign makes people learn the force of the previous warning.
Lesser tasted punishment is given so that people may return before the greater punishment makes return impossible.
With Hell brought forward, remembrance arrives at a point when it can no longer benefit the person.
Even sworn promises to believe at a sign may fail, clarifying why an already-arrived warning was not enough.
The hypocrites' cowardice and nullified works do not add a focused relation to this judgment scene.
The fate of stronger earlier peoples after clear messengers offers historical evidence against self-wronging.
Creation in successive stages does not clarify the focus's warning, judgment, or request for exit.
The promised help for messengers is a distant contrast to the wrongdoers' lack of help.
A final sign addresses people who lacked certainty in God's signs, but adds little to the focus's specific sequence.
Later severe punishment exposes denial after experienced mercy and reports what people had done.
The family dispute over remembering Joseph does not materially connect to the focus.
Those displayed before the Fire are repaid humiliating punishment for arrogance and persistent defiance.
No protector or helper exists apart from God, directly supporting the focus's denial of a helper.
Arrogance turns people from signs and makes them choose error despite seeing guidance.
Identifies the present message as a warner continuous with earlier warnings.
The purification procedure has no substantive relation to the focus's final punishment scene.
The question about a messenger's payment does not clarify the focus's warning or failed exit.
Rules for distribution of war gains do not materially illuminate the focus.
The testing of people through conflict and preservation of deeds is only a general accounting parallel.
Travel and inspect the fate of deniers, reinforcing the focus's retrospective warning from prior outcomes.
The account of attributing a granted child to partners does not clarify the focus's core scene.
At death, the wrongdoer asks to be sent back, directly anticipating the focus's impossible request to redo action.
The requested return is refused by an intervening barrier, explicitly closing the opportunity for later righteous deeds.
The inhabitants of the Fire confess that wretchedness overcame them and that they had gone astray.
The divine reply commands the condemned to remain in the Fire and ends their appeal, directly completing the blocked-exit scene.
Those standing before the Fire wish to be returned so they will no longer deny signs and will become believers.
The regretful person asks for one more return in order to become among those who do good.
After confessing their sins, the condemned explicitly ask whether any way out remains.
Fire's inhabitants ask its keepers to seek even one day of reduced punishment, a direct parallel to their futile cry.
The keepers answer by recalling the clear messengers who had already come, joining failed relief to rejected warning.
When wrongdoers see the punishment, they ask whether there is any way of return.
The inhabitants call to the keeper of Hell for termination, and the answer confirms that they will remain.
The keepers ask arriving inhabitants whether a warner had not come to them, directly supplying the focus's prior-warning frame.
The condemned admit that a warner came but that they denied him and rejected the warning.
They admit that listening or reasoning would have kept them from being companions of the Blaze.
The condemned wish for another return so that they might become believers, a close but less specific counterpart to the focus's proposed reform.
